findings.title: No structured data anywhere in the sampled pages
findings.evidence: 0 of 12 sampled pages contain JSON-LD, microdata, or RDFa.

suggested_action.summary: Add schema.org JSON-LD to key templates: Organization + WebSite on the homepage, and the page-appropriate type (Product/Offer, Article, FAQPage, LocalBusiness, BreadcrumbList) elsewhere. This is the highest-leverage discoverability fix.

findings.why: With no machine-readable markup, an assistant must infer every fact (who the brand is, what it sells, prices, dates) from prose — error-prone and rarely quoted with confidence.
findings.how_to_fix: Add schema.org JSON-LD to key templates: Organization + WebSite on the homepage, and the page-appropriate type (Product/Offer, Article, FAQPage, Course, BreadcrumbList) elsewhere.
findings.expected_impact: Makes core facts directly quotable; typically the highest-leverage discoverability fix.

findings.title: Product-like pages missing Product/Offer schema
findings.evidence: 7 of 12 page(s) (58%) look like product pages (cart/price cues) but have no Product JSON-LD, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/ebook-bundles/smashing-library/.

suggested_action.summary: Add Product JSON-LD with name, image, description, brand, and an Offer (price, priceCurrency, availability) to every product page.

findings.why: Without Product/Offer markup an assistant cannot reliably read price, availability, or rating, so the brand is left out of shopping-style answers where those facts are required.
findings.how_to_fix: Add Product JSON-LD (name, image, description, brand) with an Offer (price, priceCurrency, availability) to each product template.
findings.expected_impact: Enables price/availability to be cited in answer-engine shopping results.

findings.title: Article/blog pages missing Article schema
findings.evidence: 1 of 12 page(s) (8%) look like articles but lack Article/BlogPosting JSON-LD, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/articles/.

suggested_action.summary: Add Article/BlogPosting JSON-LD with headline, author, datePublished, and dateModified so assistants can attribute and date the content.

findings.why: Without Article markup an assistant cannot reliably attribute the piece to an author or date it, so it is trusted and cited less for topical questions.
findings.how_to_fix: Add Article/BlogPosting JSON-LD with headline, author, datePublished, and dateModified to the article template.

findings.title: Homepage lacks Organization/WebSite structured data
findings.evidence: Homepage (https://www.smashingmagazine.com/) has no Organization, LocalBusiness, or WebSite JSON-LD; detected types: none.

suggested_action.summary: Add an Organization (or LocalBusiness) node with name, url, logo, and sameAs, plus a WebSite node with name and optional SearchAction. This gives assistants a stable, unambiguous identity for the brand.

findings.why: Without an Organization/WebSite node, an assistant has no stable, machine-readable identity for the brand and cannot confidently attribute facts or citations to it.
findings.how_to_fix: Add an Organization (or LocalBusiness) node with name, url, logo, and sameAs, plus a WebSite node with name and optional SearchAction, on the homepage template.

findings.title: Pages missing an H1 heading
findings.evidence: 1 of 12 page(s) (8%) have no H1, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/articles/.

suggested_action.summary: Add exactly one descriptive H1 per page stating what the page is about in plain words.

findings.why: The H1 is the primary topic anchor a machine uses to decide what a page is about; without it the page's subject must be guessed from weaker signals.
findings.how_to_fix: Add exactly one descriptive H1 per page that states the page's topic in plain words.

findings.title: Slow server response on sampled pages
findings.evidence: 2 of 12 page(s) (17%) took over 3s to return HTML (e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/: 4778 ms).

suggested_action.summary: Investigate TTFB (caching, CDN, server work) so pages start rendering quickly; each added second measurably increases abandonment.

findings.why: A slow first byte (TTFB) delays everything downstream, so the page starts rendering late and visitors abandon before it appears.
findings.how_to_fix: Investigate TTFB — add caching/CDN, reduce per-request server work, and warm slow endpoints.

findings.title: Heading hierarchy skips levels
findings.evidence: 12 of 12 page(s) (100%) jump heading levels (e.g. H1→H3 with no H2), e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/.

suggested_action.summary: Nest headings in order (no H1→H3 jumps) so the document outline is unambiguous.

findings.why: A machine reconstructs a page's outline from heading levels; skipped levels break that nesting, so the relationship between sections is ambiguous.
findings.how_to_fix: Use headings in order (H1→H2→H3) without skipping a level; style, don't skip, to change size.

findings.title: Meta descriptions likely to be truncated
findings.evidence: 8 of 12 page(s) (67%) have a meta description longer than 160 characters, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/ebook-bundles/smashing-library/ (434 chars).

suggested_action.summary: Keep meta descriptions under ~160 characters, key fact first.

findings.why: Over-long descriptions are cut off, so the most important summary sentence may never be shown or quoted.
findings.how_to_fix: Trim descriptions to ≈50–160 characters, leading with the key fact.

findings.title: Substantial content offloaded to PDF files
findings.evidence: 3 PDF link(s) found across sampled pages.

suggested_action.summary: Publish the key information as HTML pages (the PDF can remain as a download). Ensure any essential PDFs contain real, selectable text, not scans.

findings.why: Scanned or image-only PDFs are frequently unreadable to crawlers, so any key information that lives only inside them cannot be extracted or cited.
findings.how_to_fix: Publish the key information as HTML (keep the PDF as an optional download) and ensure essential PDFs contain real, selectable text, not scans.

findings.title: Title tags outside the useful length range
findings.evidence: 9 of 12 page(s) (75%) have a <title> shorter than 15 or longer than 65 characters, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/ (75 chars).

suggested_action.summary: Keep titles roughly 15–65 characters and topic-first.

findings.why: Very short titles under-describe the page while very long ones get truncated in results and answers, so the specific topic is lost either way.
findings.how_to_fix: Rewrite titles to ≈15–65 characters: lead with the unique topic, then the brand.

notes: Crawled 12 page(s) in 60347 ms; 21 HTTP request(s). Static, read-only analysis.

opportunities.title: Add author (Person) markup to articles
opportunities.rationale: The site publishes articles but exposes no author/Person markup; explicit authorship is a trust and attribution signal assistants use.
opportunities.suggested_action: Add an author (Person, with name and optionally sameAs) to Article/BlogPosting JSON-LD and a visible byline.
opportunities.expected_impact: Better attribution and topical authority for cited content.
opportunities.evidence: Article-like content found with no author markup.

opportunities.title: Add BreadcrumbList schema on deep pages
opportunities.rationale: The site has deep pages but no BreadcrumbList markup; breadcrumbs give machines the page's place in the site hierarchy.
opportunities.suggested_action: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD (and a visible trail) on section/detail pages.
opportunities.expected_impact: Clearer site structure for machines and better orientation for visitors.
opportunities.evidence: 10 deep page(s) sampled with no BreadcrumbList schema.
